newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB says no effort made to cut off racketeer ties.
newsitem.headline: DKB says no effort made to cut off racketeer ties.

text.p: Japan's Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank said on Thursday that after an internal investigation into its loan practises, it did not find any traces of efforts made by the bank to cut off its dealings with racketeers.

Vice president Yoshiharu Mani told reporters that the bank appeared not to have followed the Commercial Code since the 1980s when the code was revised to ban payments to "sokaiya" racketeers -- corporate extortionists who threaten to disrupt shareholder meetings.
"We could not detect any trace of efforts made by the bank to cut off such ties (to racketeers)," Mani said.

A DKB spokesman also said that during a Bank of Japan inspection in 1993 and in a 1994 Finance Ministry inspection, DKB withheld details of the loans it made to a firm owned by a brother of a racketeer.

He said that it could not comment on the arrests made earlier on Thursday of four DKB officials on suspicion of loaning 11.78 billion yen to a racketeer, which prosecutors said violated the Commercial Code.
Prosectuors said that the bank made the loans through Daiwa Shinyo, a finance firm closely associated with DKB, in 51 installments from July 1994 to September 1996.
"Becauses DKB was not directly involved in those loans, I cannot comment on what happened," Mani said. He added that he was also witholding comment because the matter was still under investigation.
